- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 80), model often overcorrects downward; cap forecast decline to avoid overshoot.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.7) and price is rising, model frequently underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for next period.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show price decline, forecast should not drop below 2–3% below recent low.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overpredict late-period prices (last 5–7 days); adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% for final 5–7 days if sentiment is neutral or declining.
- If sentiment history shows alternating high-low cycles, model often misaligns with sentiment peaks; align forecast slope with sentiment direction, not just price momentum.
